title: Partition a mixed number: wholes and a fraction in a part-whole diagram beside a bar model of the wholes (fractions:mixed_numbers_intro, NEW)

template.also: A NEW DRAWING (first build at Opus medium, IMPROVEMENT_PLAN Q-S1): a new `frac-model` task `partition` (payload below) that draws (1) the mixed number's bar model as STACKED whole bars plus the part bar (WRM R50 'bar models of mixed numbers stacked'; frac-model draws values past 1 as a ROW of wholes today, RP-92, which cannot sit beside a diagram at 52 / 56 mm a whole) and (2) the part-whole diagram of RP-60 with a fraction slot in a part box. The part-whole grammar is copied from cells/bond.js (whole box over part boxes, 0.75 pt joins); the fraction slot and mixed-number glyph from cells/equation.js `frac` / `mixed` (TY-7, WDS 3.2). Generator: gen-fractions.js (new branch `mixed_numbers_intro`); provider js/modules/sheet/providers/ (fractions provider: strings, workedSteps, wrongAnswer, footprint); screen-cell.js draws the same cell on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz. Mock: design/cards/mixed-partition/mock.html, mock-M.png, mock-L.png (built from sheet/tokens.js SIZES M / L).

summary: ONE new skill, fractions:mixed_numbers_intro 'Partition a Mixed Number' (WRM Y4.B7.S3; school grade 3). Each cell prints a mixed number (2 3/4) in the whole box of a part-whole diagram; the pupil writes the wholes (2) in the left part box and the fraction (3/4) in the right part box. On the model steps the mixed number's bar model stands left of the diagram: one fully shaded bar per whole and one part-shaded bar, stacked with 3 mm gaps (WRM R50). The model is a hint that fades; the part-whole diagram, its two part boxes and their labels 'wholes' / 'fraction' are structural and stay. Later steps: three parts (2 3/4 = 1 + 1 + 3/4, 4.NF.B.3b), the reverse (parts given: write the mixed number), and the equation form '2 3/4 = [ ] + [ ]/[ ]'. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing.
teaches: 4.NF.B.3b (decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator, including a mixed number: 2 1/8 = 1 + 1 + 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8) - primary; 3.NF.A.1 (a fraction as a quantity formed by parts of size 1/b; the part bar). EE: M.EE.4.NF.3 (linked to 4.NF.B.3: 'Differentiate between whole and half'), M.EE.3.NF.1 (linked to 3.NF.A.1: 'Differentiate a fractional part from a whole'). WRM: Y4.B7.S3 'Partition a mixed number' (verdict gap today; build list frac_beyond_1; Y4.json missing: 'partitioning a mixed number into wholes and a fraction (2 3/4 = 2 + 3/4 = 1 + 1 + 3/4) with a part-whole model'). The same proposal also names Y4.B7.S2 (count beyond 1), S5 (compare and order mixed numbers) and S12; those parts are NOT on this card (see Q3). School grade 3 (lead-confirmed: WRM Year 4 = grade 3), although CCSS places 4.NF.B.3b in grade 4 (Q2).
research: Searched 2026-11-20 (WebSearch; no logins - a WebFetch cannot hold a session, so the MathWorksheets4Kids and IXL member pages were not opened; nothing was copied). MathWorksheets4Kids (primary): its public mixed-number pages model a mixed number as whole shapes plus a part shape and ask to write the mixed number or the improper fraction; no 'partition' set was found publicly. IXL (secondary): grade 4 'decompose fractions' / 'decompose fractions into unit fractions' and 'mixed numbers' skill names (public list only): write the sum, multiple choice of decompositions. Year 4 sets found by search: White Rose Spring Block 3 Step 3 (part-whole models and bar models; partition into a whole number and a fraction, then into a whole and a mixed number, or a mixed number and a fraction); Classroom Secrets 'Partition a Mixed Number' varied fluency (fraction shapes, bar models, complete the part-whole model; reasoning: 'which partition is wrong?'); Oak National 'compose and decompose mixed numbers' (a mixed number = a whole-number part and a fractional part); NCETM PD 3.05 'working across one whole'. K5 Learning / Math-Drills: mixed-number pictures to name, no partition set. Sequence taken (not pacing): the bar picture beside the part-whole -> part-whole alone -> three parts (1 + 1 + 3/4) -> the reverse (parts to the mixed number) -> the equation -> flexible partitions (1 + 1 3/4) as stretch. Where our standards override: black and white with the single grey for shaded parts, Andika, one problem a boxed cell, 2-4 cells a page with the model (research fits 6-12), labels printed on the part boxes (no word to compose), no circle 'pizza' pictures by default (Q6).
problemTypes: partition (default task): the mixed number printed in the whole box; write the wholes and the fraction in the two part boxes (one answer: both parts, graded as one 'partition' answer, SL-7). With the bar model on the model steps.

ones (task 'ones', 4.NF.B.3b): three or more part boxes - each whole as 1 and the fraction (2 3/4 = 1 + 1 + 3/4); the part boxes are all boxes (SL-3), the count of boxes = wholes + 1 (so it never hints at a wrong count: it is structural, the bars already show the wholes; Q5).

compose (task 'compose', the reverse; WRM S2 naming the mixed number): the parts printed (2 and 3/4), the pupil writes the mixed number in the whole box (the mixed-number slot of WDS 6: a whole box beside a fraction bar).
equation (response form 'eq'): no diagram; '2 3/4 = [ ] + [ ]/[ ]' on the equation frame (the same parts, the mixed number printed left of '='). The faded paper form and the exit-slip form.
which is wrong? (error analysis / True or False? only, from the provider): a printed partition with one misconception (2 3/4 = 2 + 3/8; 2 3/4 = 3 + 2/4) - true or false, or fix it.
progression: 1 halves and quarters, 1 whole (1 1/2, 1 3/4): bar model beside the part-whole -> 2 two wholes (2 1/4) -> 3 thirds, fifths, sixths, eighths (denominators 3-8) -> 4 three wholes (3 2/5; 4 bars stacked) - one change a step: the denominator set OR the number of wholes, never both (P-1).

5 model faded: the part-whole alone, two across (the scaffold change alone, on step-3 numbers) -> 6 wholes to 5 without a model (a model of 6 bars does not fit a cell) -> 7 task 'ones' (1 + 1 + 3/4) with the model back on for its first page (a new task brings its scaffold back, P-7) -> 8 task 'compose' (the reverse) -> 9 the equation form (the exit-slip form) -> stretch: flexible partitions (2 3/4 = 1 + 1 3/4 = 2 1/4 + 2/4; Q8: stretch / reason-it only, not a practice task).

Structural (stay on every item of every step): the part-whole diagram, its joins, the part boxes and their printed labels 'wholes' / 'fraction' (RP-71: the pupil fills numbers, not words), the fraction bar inside the fraction box. Hint (fades, in this order): the shaded bar model (Guided keeps it on its Model only after step 4), then nothing else - the labels never fade (an ELL pupil keeps the words).

drawing.sizes: Mixed number in the whole box: the whole digit at the working digit size 22 / 28 pt (M / L), the fraction at the fraction size 16 / 20 pt over a 1.5 pt bar (WDS 3.2: 'Whole part of a mixed number stays at working digit size'; TY-7). Whole box 34 x 22 mm (M) / 40 x 26 mm (L), 1.5 pt, square (printed, not a writing place; RP-60 the whole box heavier). Part boxes (writing places): wholes box B(1) + 6 = 20 mm wide (M and L) x (2 Hw + 8) = 24 / 28 mm tall; fraction box B(2) + 6 = 20 / 23 mm wide, the same height, holding a 1.5 pt fraction bar B(2) = 14 / 17 mm wide with a writing zone Hw (8 / 10 mm) above and below (WDS 6 'Fraction bar'); 0.75 pt, slot radius 1.25 / 1.5 mm (SL-11; Q4). Joins 0.75 pt from the whole box's foot to each part box's top; 12 mm drop; the part boxes 22 mm apart. Labels 'wholes' / 'fraction' at zone-label size 10 / 12 pt under the part boxes. Bar model: each whole a fraction bar 52 x 16 mm (M) / 56 x 18 mm (L) (WDS 11.2 minimums), outline 1.5 pt, dividers 0.75 pt, shaded parts flat grey #949494 from the left (RP-90; hatch in photocopy-safe mode), bars stacked with a 3 mm gap (RP-92's gap, stacked not in a row), one bar per whole plus the part bar; denominators 2-8 keep every part >= 6.5 mm (RP-93). Measured on the mock: the model cell is 70 mm tall at M with 2 wholes, 80 mm at L.
notes: Payload (new frac-model task 'partition'): {task: 'partition', w, n, d, form: 'two'|'ones'|'compose'|'eq', model: 'bar'|'none', labels: true}; answer {w, n, d} (partition / eq), {parts: [1, 1, {n, d}]} (ones), {w, n, d} written in the whole box (compose). Generator deals w 1-3 (model on) or 1-5 (model off), d from the denominator set, n 1..d-1 (never 0: then it is a whole number; never d: then it is w + 1), no repeat of (w, n, d) on a page, the answer position irrelevant (two fixed boxes), each attribute its own seeded draw (L10).

Answer slots (VQ-2, SL-7): ONE graded answer a cell - the two part boxes together (partition), all part boxes (ones), the mixed-number slot (compose), the three boxes of the equation (eq); each box is a typed input on screen with data-mq-expect, the answer judged as a whole (all boxes right). Slot widths from the widest answer the band can give (SL-2): wholes B(1), fraction B(2) wide enough for 1 digit at denominators <= 8 (L3: the width never shows the answer).

Layout: model cells are full-width rows (bars left after the tab keep-out, the part-whole centred in the rest, CL-6 the response always in the part boxes); model-off cells two across. Capacity (PROPOSED Q9, measured at build by ws-empty-band / ws-options-verify --render; content never shrinks): model on, wholes <= 2: M 3 / L 2 a page; wholes 3 (4 bars): M 2 / L 2; model off: M 6 (2 x 3) / L 4 (2 x 2); ones form +1 part box: the same rows; equation form: M 8 (2 x 4) / L 6 (2 x 3). WDS 12.1 wide-visual rows 4 / 3 is the ceiling; the model is taller than a number line, so it holds fewer. EB-SIDE risk: the model row leaves ~30 mm white right of the diagram at M (mock-M.png) - the diagram is centred in the space after the bars to keep each side under 30 % (Q10).
Key (AK-1, AK-2): the same cell with the answers in the pupil's own boxes at the digit / fraction size in key ink; the bars are already shaded (they show the printed number, not the answer).

Screen twin: the same drawing at --mq-k2 px; part boxes are 48 px touch targets (tablets, plan item 7); the fraction box is two inputs (numerator over denominator) on its bar; at 820-1024 px the model row stacks the bars above the diagram if the card is narrower than bars + diagram. No production becomes a choice on screen (SL-7, SCC-T15).

Instruction strings (contract.js library, NEW, <= 8 words, PROPOSED Q11): 'mixed-partition' 'Split the mixed number into wholes and a fraction.' (as on the mock); 'mixed-ones' 'Split it into ones and a fraction.'; 'mixed-compose' 'Write the mixed number.'; 'mixed-eq' 'Write the wholes and the fraction.'. iCan: 'I can split a mixed number into wholes and a fraction.'

Say frame (the model's Say: band, oral, never a slot): '2 3/4 is 2 wholes and 3/4.' / '2 and 3/4 make 2 3/4.' (compose) / '2 3/4 is 1 + 1 + 3/4.' (ones). Lesson routine (PROPOSED, prereqs.js lesson data): 1 Read the mixed number. 2 Count the whole bars. Write the wholes. 3 Look at the last bar. Write the fraction. 4 Say it. Chant: 'Wholes first. Then the part.'

Misconception-driven items for error analysis, True or False? and Reason It come from the provider's wrongAnswer list (section 6): each wrong partition is a real error, never the right answer (ws-providers-unit WRONG-DIFFERS per box, L27).

openQuestions.q: Accept every role, host and option decision marked PROPOSED in section 7a, and the new drawing as mocked (mock-M.png / mock-L.png)?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, all as proposed; first build at Opus medium (a new drawing).

openQuestions.q: Grade and primary standard: CCSS puts the mixed-number decomposition in 4.NF.B.3b (grade 4); the school teaches it in WRM Year 4 = grade 3. Grade property and the primary tag?
openQuestions.recommended: grade 3 (the school's grade, lead-confirmed); SKILL_STANDARDS primary 4.NF.B.3b, then 3.NF.A.1; EE M.EE.4.NF.3, M.EE.3.NF.1.

openQuestions.q: frac_beyond_1 also covers Y4.B7.S2 (count beyond 1), S5 (compare and order) and S12 (a number line). Build them into this skill?
openQuestions.recommended: No: this card builds S3 only (the brief's scope). The compose preset covers S2's 'name the mixed number' part; the S2 counting line, S5 compare / order and S12 stay on the build list as frac_beyond_1 (narrowed) / frac_compare_gt1 / vis_frac_bar_modes.

openQuestions.q: Part boxes: RP-60 says part-whole boxes are square-cornered; SL-11 (owner 2026-09-25) rounds every writing box. Which wins on the part boxes?
openQuestions.recommended: SL-11 (the later owner ruling, and the part boxes are writing places): part boxes rounded 1.25 / 1.5 mm; the printed whole box stays square. Add a one-line note to RP-60.

openQuestions.q: Task 'ones' prints wholes + 1 part boxes: does the box count give away the number of wholes?
openQuestions.recommended: No: the mixed number is printed and its whole part is the count; the box count is structural, the same rule as SL-2 (every item's boxes from its own structure). Keep it, and keep the model on for the first 'ones' page.

openQuestions.q: Offer a circle model (WRM also draws whole circles)?
openQuestions.recommended: No for now: a circle is 42 / 50 mm, so three circles beside the diagram do not fit a cell at M or L, and one model (bars) keeps one picture across the unit (S5 / S7 use bars too). Revisit with vis_frac_bar_modes.

openQuestions.q: Which options are ALSO findable preset skills (10-17 rule)?
openQuestions.recommended: One preset: mnTask 'compose' -> fractions:write_mixed_from_parts 'Write a Mixed Number from Wholes and a Fraction' (grade 3, 4.NF.B.3b + 3.NF.A.1, WRM Y4.B7.S2 partial). 'ones', 'eq', model none and the number-size controls stay plain options.
Stretch and Reason It pages only (the provider deals them there); not a practice task this round.

openQuestions.q: Capacity per page before measurement (section 3 notes)?
openQuestions.recommended: Model on: M 3 / L 2 (wholes <= 2), M 2 / L 2 (3 wholes); model off: M 6 / L 4; equation form M 8 / L 6. Measured at build; the card is resigned only if a number falls.

openQuestions.q: The model row leaves white right of the diagram at M (EB-SIDE risk). Fix?
openQuestions.recommended: Centre the diagram in the width after the bars (as on the mock) and measure EB-SIDE; if a side still passes 30 %, widen the part-whole spacing (gap 22 -> 30 mm) rather than shrink anything.

openQuestions.q: The four new instruction strings and the iCan as worded in section 3?
